name: Glean
product: Work AI platform combining permission-aware enterprise search, a knowledge graph, retrieval-augmented generation and agents across company systems.
targetCustomer: Large enterprises with fragmented knowledge and SaaS estates
buyer: CIO, CTO, Chief AI Officer or Head of Knowledge Management
traction: Glean reported surpassing $300M ARR in May 2026, 15 months after reaching $100M ARR, and nearly doubling its Fortune 500 customer count year over year.
notes: Its defensibility comes from permission-aware connectors, enterprise context and production distribution, not a proprietary frontier model. ARR and customer-growth metrics are company-reported.

name: Hebbia
product: Matrix is a multi-agent research workspace that analyzes large document sets and produces cited tables, memos, presentations and spreadsheets.
targetCustomer: Financial institutions, professional-services firms and other document-intensive enterprises
buyer: Head of Research, CIO, COO or business-unit leader
traction: Hebbia says Matrix is used by more than 40% of the world's largest asset managers by assets under management, alongside investment banks and professional-services firms.
notes: The finance wedge creates valuable workflow depth and willingness to pay; the product is less horizontal in practice than its general document interface suggests. Adoption is company-reported and funding total comes from a secondary aggregate.

name: Writer
product: Full-stack enterprise AI platform spanning Palmyra language models, knowledge retrieval, agent orchestration and no-code application development.
targetCustomer: Large enterprises deploying governed generative-AI workflows
buyer: CIO, CTO, Chief AI Officer or business transformation leader
traction: Writer lists hundreds of enterprise customers, including Accenture, Mars, Marriott, Uber and Vanguard.
notes: A rare vertically integrated application vendor that also trains enterprise-focused models. That breadth raises technical depth but also capital intensity; customer count is company-reported.

name: Dust
product: Model-agnostic platform for building shared enterprise agents connected to internal knowledge and business tools.
targetCustomer: Technology companies and enterprise business teams
buyer: CIO, Head of AI, COO or functional leader
traction: Dust reported 240% net revenue retention and zero customer churn during 2025.
notes: Funding is a lower bound because the announcement states more than $60M raised. Its model-agnostic posture and collaborative agent workspace are useful, but connector depth and distribution are more defensible than underlying model IP; retention metrics are company-reported.

name: Granola
product: Bot-free AI notepad that transcribes meetings, enriches user notes and builds searchable team context across conversations.
targetCustomer: Knowledge workers, teams and enterprises
buyer: Individual user, team leader, Head of Operations or CIO
traction: Granola names Vanta, Gusto, Thumbtack and Asana among customers as it expands from individual notes to shared team context.
notes: The low-friction notepad workflow is a strong PLG wedge, but speech and frontier-model suppliers can compress technical differentiation. Customer data is not treated as vendor-owned proprietary data.

name: Gamma
product: AI design partner for generating and editing presentations, documents, websites and social content from prompts or source material.
targetCustomer: Individuals, teams and enterprises producing business content
buyer: Individual user, marketing leader, enablement leader or CIO
fundingDisplay: ~$90M announced; latest round includes secondary shares
latestRound: Series B, Nov 2025 ($68M including a secondary component)
traction: Gamma reported $100M ARR, profitability, 70M users and more than 400M created assets in Nov 2025.
notes: The reported roughly $90M total includes a secondary component in the $68M Series B, so not all headline proceeds were new company capital. Distribution and automated design are stronger moats than model IP; all operating metrics are company-reported.

name: Read AI
product: AI assistant that summarizes and searches meetings, email and messages, with a digital-twin agent that can act on a user's communication context.
targetCustomer: Knowledge workers, teams and enterprises
buyer: Individual user, Head of Productivity, COO or CIO
traction: Read AI reported more than 5M monthly active users in 2026; at the Series B it reported 100,000 new accounts per week and 81% first-month retention.
notes: Cross-channel context and distribution improve the meeting-notes wedge, but consent, recording governance and data-retention controls are central enterprise risks. Usage and retention are company-reported.

name: Notion
product: Collaborative workspace for docs, wikis and databases augmented with enterprise search, meeting notes and configurable agents that work across connected tools.
targetCustomer: Individuals, teams and enterprises
buyer: Team leader, COO, CIO or Head of Knowledge Management
latestRound: Series C, Oct 2021 ($275M); $270M secondary tender in Jan 2026 excluded
traction: Notion reported more than 1M custom agents created by May 2026, after an initial early-access cohort of more than 21,000 testers.
notes: Its installed workspace, user distribution and embedded data model are the moat; technical depth is lower because public evidence does not show proprietary frontier-model research. The $270M 2026 employee-share tender is secondary liquidity, not company funding, and is excluded.

name: Sierra
product: Enterprise platform for deploying governed customer-facing agents across messaging and voice channels, including transactional tool use and outcome measurement.
targetCustomer: Large consumer-facing enterprises
buyer: Chief Customer Officer, Chief Digital Officer or CIO
latestRound: Series E, May 2026 ($950M at more than $15B valuation)
traction: Sierra reported serving more than 40% of the Fortune 50 and handling billions of customer interactions by May 2026.
notes: Deep action integrations, evaluation and enterprise deployment support justify high vertical-integration and technical scores. The company still depends on frontier-model suppliers, and its unusually high valuation and all traction metrics are company-reported.

name: Decagon
product: Enterprise customer-support agent platform for chat, email and voice, using Agent Operating Procedures to compile natural-language policies into executable workflows.
targetCustomer: Digital businesses and global enterprises with high-volume support
buyer: Chief Customer Officer, VP Customer Experience or CIO
traction: Decagon reported adding more than 100 global enterprise customers during the fiscal year preceding its Jan 2026 Series D.
notes: Agent Operating Procedures are a credible control-plane differentiation, but independent reliability benchmarks are sparse and the category is crowded. Funding total is a secondary aggregate; adoption is company-reported.

sources.label: Series C and Agent Operating Procedures

name: Parloa
product: Agent-management platform for creating, testing and operating enterprise customer-service agents across voice and messaging channels.
targetCustomer: Large enterprises and contact-center operators
buyer: Chief Customer Officer, VP Contact Center or CIO
traction: Parloa reported exceeding $50M ARR in 2025 with 150% net revenue retention.
notes: Low-latency telephony, testing and multilingual enterprise deployment provide real workflow depth. The company remains exposed to contact-center incumbents and frontier speech/model suppliers; funding is a stated lower bound and operating metrics are company-reported.

name: PolyAI
product: Enterprise voice-assistant platform that automates high-volume customer-service calls while integrating with contact-center and back-office systems.
targetCustomer: Large enterprises with high-volume contact centers
buyer: Chief Customer Officer, VP Contact Center or CIO
traction: PolyAI says its voice assistants resolve millions of customer-service inquiries for enterprise brands.
notes: Its academic speech and dialogue heritage supports a high technical-depth score, while public current revenue metrics are limited. Funding is a company-stated lower bound; frontier speech APIs and CCaaS incumbents can compress differentiation.

name: Clay
subsector: GTM data enrichment and sales workflows
product: GTM development environment that combines data enrichment, buying signals, agentic web research and multichannel workflow automation.
targetCustomer: Growth teams, sales organizations and revenue operations
buyer: CRO, VP Growth or Head of Revenue Operations
latestRound: Series C, Aug 2025 ($100M at $3.1B valuation); Jan 2026 tender excluded
traction: Clay reported reaching $100M ARR in 2025, with more than 200% enterprise net revenue retention and no enterprise churn.
notes: Primary funding is estimated as the roughly $277M announced total less $75M of disclosed secondary tenders; exact primary proceeds are therefore approximate. The moat is the integration and enrichment ecosystem plus distribution, not proprietary model research; operating metrics are company-reported.

name: Gong
product: Revenue AI operating system that captures customer interactions, builds a revenue graph and supports coaching, forecasting and agentic sales workflows.
targetCustomer: Mid-market and enterprise revenue organizations
buyer: CRO, VP Sales or Head of Revenue Operations
traction: Gong reported more than $500M ARR, greater than 55% year-over-year growth and about 5,000 customers in May 2026.
notes: A mature reference rather than an early startup: its longitudinal interaction corpus, revenue graph and embedded system-of-record workflows support a strong moat. Revenue and customer metrics are company-reported; call recording creates privacy and governance obligations.

name: Unify
subsector: Outbound sales agents and GTM orchestration
product: GTM orchestration platform that combines intent signals, enrichment, AI account research, personalized messaging and outbound sequences.
targetCustomer: B2B growth, sales and revenue-operations teams
buyer: CRO, VP Growth or Head of Revenue Operations
traction: Unify reported more than 4,000 deployed AI agents and 10,000 positive replies during 2025; its own agents generated $27.5M of qualified pipeline for Unify.
notes: Cumulative funding is the sum of the disclosed $6.6M seed, $12M Series A and $40M Series B. AI outbound is crowded and generated copy is weakly defensible; signal, enrichment and workflow orchestration are the substantive layer. Traction is company-reported and includes internal pipeline, not recognized revenue.

name: Rox
product: Revenue-agent platform that helps enterprise sellers plan, prioritize, research, engage and monitor complex accounts using connected CRM and company context.
targetCustomer: Enterprise B2B sales organizations
buyer: CRO or VP Enterprise Sales
fundingDisplay: $50M disclosed plus a later undisclosed round
latestRound: Undisclosed round in 2025, reported Mar 2026; latest disclosed amount was $50M in 2024
traction: Rox names customers including Intel, Bosch, Hitachi, GitLab, Ramp and MongoDB; TechCrunch reported the company projected closing 2025 at about $8M ARR.
notes: The $50M is a lower bound because a later financing amount was not disclosed. The $1.2B valuation and projected $8M 2025 ARR are secondary reporting, not directly comparable to audited realized revenue. Rox explicitly positions itself as an application company rather than an AI-research lab.

name: Ramp
product: Integrated finance-operations platform spanning corporate cards, spend controls, procurement, travel, bill pay, treasury and accounting automation.
targetCustomer: Businesses from startups to large enterprises
buyer: CFO, Controller or Head of Procurement
traction: Ramp reported more than 70,000 business customers and 170% year-over-year growth in transaction volume at its Jun 2026 Series F.
notes: A mature fintech reference, not a pure AI company. Transaction data, payment rails, licenses and integrated workflows create a stronger moat than its LLM layer. The funding figure is the company's stated equity total and excludes warehouse, card and other debt facilities; metrics are company-reported.

name: Rillet
product: AI-native ERP and general ledger automating close, multi-entity accounting, revenue recognition, reporting and finance-system integrations.
targetCustomer: High-growth and mid-market companies with complex accounting
buyer: CFO or Controller
traction: Rillet reported more than 400 customers in Apr 2026 and announced an alliance with EY US for implementations and go-to-market support.
notes: Replacing the ledger creates much deeper lock-in and data integrity requirements than an overlay. Accounting controls and implementation partnerships are advantages, but migration, auditability and trust are material adoption constraints; funding is a stated lower bound and customer count is company-reported.

name: Numeric
product: Finance platform for close management, reconciliations, flux analysis, technical accounting and consolidated financial data.
targetCustomer: Controllers and accounting teams at public and growth companies
buyer: Controller, Chief Accounting Officer or CFO
traction: Numeric reports hundreds of public and private company customers, including Brex, Plaid and Wealthfront.
notes: Numeric is an accounting workflow and data layer around incumbent ledgers, so switching costs are lower than for a full ERP replacement. Auditability and factual accuracy matter more than fluent generation; customer count is company-reported. Founding year is from public company-profile data.

name: Basis
product: Domain-specific AI agents for accounting firms, automating document-heavy accounting, tax and audit workflows under human supervision.
targetCustomer: Accounting and professional-services firms
buyer: Managing Partner, COO or Accounting Practice Leader
traction: Basis has announced accounting-firm deployments including Baker Tilly, but publicly quantified production-volume or revenue metrics remain limited.
notes: Funding is the sum of the disclosed $3.8M seed, $34M Series A and $100M Series B. Domain-specific controls and evaluations are credible differentiation, but funding has moved faster than transparent adoption evidence; professional-services workflow depth also makes this less horizontal than generic back-office software.
